parameters.No symmetry: Use the existing planar initializer and independent relaxation. No reflection is required. This is the default and preserves generation for templates without symmetry settings.
parameters.Face only symmetry: Choose corresponding planar faces for paired zones using matching generation settings, then release their coordinate constraints. With no active position magnets, the seed chooses the orientation across 360 degrees. Forces, random perturbations and node positions can evolve independently during relaxation, while crossing prevention preserves the initial face choices. Paired magnets may have different targets. Growth, walls and resources are unrestricted.
parameters.Embedding symmetry: Keep paired zone centers mirrored throughout initial placement and every relaxation step. The reflection must match zone and connection generation settings as well as topology. Axis nodes stay on a line through the map center. With no active position magnets, the seed chooses the orientation across 360 degrees. Forces, perturbations and movement limits are coupled, but growth, walls and resources may still differ. Compatible magnet targets determine the axis; random rotation turns the axis with them.
parameters.Complete symmetry: Keep the embedding symmetric and mirror zone ownership, walls, passage openings, noise and final resource tiles. Paired zones stay on their respective sides of the axis; fixed axis zones can span it. The axis does not add walls or blending: configured rules apply at real borders. Mirrored pairs share resource percentile normalization to avoid a low-resource seam. One half is authoritative and its reflected zone IDs fill the opposite half. Square maps support horizontal, vertical and both diagonal axes, selected by the seed when no position magnets guide orientation. Non-square maps support horizontal and vertical axes. Random magnet rotation chooses fitting grid-compatible orientations. Paired zones, shared connections and directed rules must have matching generation settings; conflicts appear in the top-menu !. Dense layouts may require a larger resolution so every zone seed can be represented.
parameters.Random magnet rotation: Rotate all position magnet targets together around the map center using an angle chosen from the seed. Their distances to each other and the center, and their forces, stay the same. Outside Complete symmetry, angles across 360 degrees are considered if every active target fits. Complete symmetry chooses fitting rigid rotations aligning the axis horizontally, vertically or diagonally on square maps; non-square maps allow horizontal and vertical axes. Near-corner targets limit available angles. Rotation uses map cells so rectangular maps also preserve distances. Disabled by default; saved targets and the editor diagram are never rotated.
parameters.Magnet: Attract this zone toward its own saved target inside the map frame during generation. This force is independent of susceptibility to the shared central magnet. Targets guide the initial drawing before crossing-preserving relaxation, so a leaf can start on the intended side of a surrounding cycle. Turn it off here or single-click the zone in Magnet mode.
parameters.Magnet force: The positive strength holding this zone toward its own target position: 0.1 to 100, with 1 as the default. The minimum remains enabled; switch the magnet off explicitly. In Magnet mode, drag outward to increase force, or grab off-center and drag toward the zone center to reduce it to 0.1. Force and its glow do not depend on camera zoom.
parameters.Magnet position: Normalized map coordinates: (0, 0) is the frame's top left, (1, 1) its bottom right, and (0.5, 0.5) its center. Derived from the zone center and the square map frame. The frame follows the bounds of all zones, including non-magnets, and cannot shrink below them. Targets outside the frame are inactive. Generation uses the saved target rather than raw visualizer coordinates. Attraction is a soft preference; bounds, connections and other forces can prevent an exact match.
parameters.Template name: The template's display name in the editor and generator. This does not rename the JSON file.
parameters.Node ID: A unique non-negative whole number identifying this zone. Changing it updates every connection and directed rule that refers to the zone.
parameters.Radius: A positive relative size weight. Larger values give this zone a larger share of growth seeds and influence embedding spacing. It is not a guaranteed final area. The editor square grows with this value.
parameters.Susceptibility: Magnetic attraction to the map's center. Positive values attract, negative values repel, and zero is neutral. Planarity and map boundaries can limit movement.
parameters.Custom wall resource: Choose a material for generated boundary walls. When disabled, walls use Cliff rock.
parameters.Wall material: The resource used to paint generated walls between zones, including walls between sand zones.
parameters.Octave count: Use one to three noise layers. Removing a layer also removes its weights from every zone.
parameters.Minimum radius: The smallest noise feature radius for this octave. Must be positive and no larger than the maximum radius.
parameters.Maximum radius: The largest noise feature radius for this octave. Larger radii generally produce broader resource patches.
parameters.Override: Enable an explicit noise weight for this zone and octave. An omitted weight defaults to zero.
parameters.Weight: This octave's non-negative contribution to the zone's resource noise. Larger weights make that layer more influential. An omitted weight is zero.
parameters.Material: The resource assigned to this noise interval. Its color fills the corresponding vertical band in the editor square.
parameters.Start threshold: The lower bound of this resource's noise interval, from 0 to 1. Threshold zero is the bottom of the editor square. All positive intervals together must cover 0 to 1 without gaps or overlaps.
parameters.End threshold: The upper bound of this resource's noise interval, from its start to 1. Threshold one is the top of the square. Match adjoining boundaries to avoid gaps or overlaps.
parameters.Restrict map dimensions: Optionally limit the map sizes available in the Generator tab. Without restrictions, each side can be any even number from 32 to 128.
parameters.Set min: Enable an inclusive minimum bound. Width and height must be even and between 32 and 128; aspect ratio is width divided by height.
parameters.Set max: Enable an inclusive maximum bound. The restrictions must allow at least one supported map size.
parameters.min: Inclusive lower bound. Width and height use even cell counts (32 to 128). Aspect ratio uses width / height, for example 1 for a square or 2 for twice as wide as tall.
parameters.max: Inclusive upper bound. It must be at least the minimum and allow at least one even width/height pair.
parameters.Minimum pass width: The minimum width of openings through the generated border, in cells. Cannot exceed the maximum. On the canvas, passages are transparent gaps.
parameters.Maximum pass width: The maximum width of border openings, in cells. This affects passages, not the distance between zone centers.
parameters.Minimum wall length: The minimum length of wall between passages, in cells. Cannot exceed the maximum. Black segments represent walls on the canvas.
parameters.Maximum wall length: The maximum length of wall between passages, in cells. Zero wall lengths allow continuous openings.
parameters.Resource blending: Enable resource mixing across this shared border. This shared setting applies to both zones; directed rules below control each direction separately.
parameters.Blend distance: The non-negative whole-number reach of shared resource blending across this border, in cells. Zero disables this shared reach.
parameters.Preferred center distance: Enable a preferred generation distance between the two zone seeds. Disabling it uses radius-derived spacing. The editor's drawn positions never set this distance.
parameters.Center distance: A positive target distance in map cells. This is a soft preference: planarity, bounds and other forces may prevent an exact match.
parameters.Custom distance weight: Override the strength of the center-distance preference. The default is 1.
parameters.Distance weight: The non-negative importance of fitting the desired center distance. Larger values prioritize this edge; zero disables its distance objective without removing the connection.
parameters.Enable directed rule: Enable resource influence from the first displayed zone to the second. The reverse rule is independent and requires the same shared connection.
parameters.Intake distance: A non-negative whole-number distance controlling the spatial reach of this directed resource intake during blending.
parameters.Guaranteed area: A non-negative whole-number budget of cells for guaranteed directed resource influence near this border. This is not a guarantee of the zone's total final area.
parameters.Bonus value: A non-negative weight added to resource influence by this directed rule. Larger bonuses strengthen the rule's contribution during blending.
parameters.default: Configure this template parameter. Apply validates the value before changing the document.

text.symmetry_warning: The selected symmetry mode needs a certified planar reflection with matching paired zone and connection generation settings. Embedding symmetry also needs compatible magnet targets. Complete symmetry additionally needs a grid-compatible axis: horizontal, vertical or either diagonal on square maps, and horizontal or vertical on non-square maps. Fix the reported issue or choose No symmetry in Global settings. You can still edit and save the template. Crossed canvas lines alone do not prevent graph symmetry. Search-limit messages are inconclusive rather than proof that symmetry is absent.
text.selection_mode:
Selection mode (V)
Ctrl-click or drag a box to select multiple zones.
text.edge_mode:
Edge mode (E)
Click two zones to connect them.
Or select a zone, hold Shift and click another.
text.magnet_mode:
Magnet mode (M / hold Alt)
Single-click a zone to toggle its position magnet.
Drag outward to increase force; drag toward its center to decrease.
Wheel resizes the map frame; Ctrl+wheel zooms the camera.
text.fit_magnet_frame: Reset the square map frame to fit all zone squares, including non-magnets. The frame is centered on the diagram bounds and cannot shrink below this size. Resizing changes normalized targets, not canvas positions.
text.fit_graph: Fit all zones in view (F / Home)
text.empty_canvas: Double-click the canvas to create your first node.
text.dimensions: Width and height must be even, from 32 to 128. Aspect ratio is width / height.
text.resource_intervals: Positive intervals must cover 0 to 1 without gaps or overlaps. Split an interval to add a resource row.
text.save_changes: Save your template changes before continuing?
text.generation_selected: Template selected. Open the Generator tab to generate a map.
text.map_square: Square map: both sides change together.
text.map_adjust_other: The other side adjusts to keep this shape.
text.map_adjusted: Size adjusted to fit this template.
text.topology_warning: This graph topology is non-planar: its connections cannot be drawn without crossings, regardless of node placement. Remove or change connections to restore planarity. Auto place is disabled and generation cannot use this topology. Crossed lines in a manual drawing alone do not mean the topology is non-planar.
text.auto_place: Arrange nodes as a compact diagram. Prefer rectangular boundaries, symmetric rows and columns, and horizontal, vertical or 45-degree connections. Grid snapping preserves topology and avoids node overlaps. Leave room for one complete edge pattern at 100% zoom, then fit the whole graph in view. Only visualizer positions change; Undo restores the previous arrangement.
text.auto_place_disabled: Auto place is unavailable while the graph has a topology warning. Remove or change connections until the warning clears.
text.auto_placed: Nodes placed automatically. Undo restores the previous positions.

help.title: Symmetry modes
paragraphs: Global settings > Symmetry offers four radio choices. No symmetry preserves the existing generation. Face only symmetry starts paired zones in corresponding planar faces and then allows independent positional relaxation; both members start inside or outside their corresponding cycles, while their shapes and distances can evolve separately. Every symmetry mode matches parsed zone and connection generation data, including radii, susceptibility, resources, octave weights, passages, blending, geometry preferences and directed rules. IDs and canvas coordinates do not define the pairing.

Embedding symmetry keeps paired centers mirrored throughout initial placement and relaxation, including perturbations, forces and movement limits. Axis zones remain on a line through the center. Face only and Embedding symmetry retain seeded orientation across 360 degrees when there are no active position magnets. Magnet targets guide orientation when present. Growth, smoothing, walls and resources can still be asymmetric.

Complete symmetry uses embedding symmetry plus an authoritative half of the tile grid. Paired zones stay on their own sides while fixed axis zones can span the line. Walls and configured resource blending follow real zone borders; the axis itself adds neither. Paired zones share percentile normalization, including diagonal tiles, so the seam does not force minimum-threshold resources. It mirrors zone IDs to their partners, together with walls, passage openings, noise and resources, so every final tile has a matching reflected tile. Square maps support horizontal, vertical and both diagonal axes; non-square maps support horizontal and vertical axes. The seed chooses the axis when no position magnets guide it. Paired generation settings must match; incompatible settings are explained by !. Random magnet rotation selects fitting grid-compatible orientations in this mode. Dense node seeds may need a larger map.

The top-menu ! explains a missing planar reflection, unmatched generation data, incompatible magnets, or an inconclusive search limit. These differ from non-planarity. Drafts can still be saved. Earlier templates with embedding/symmetrical: true keep Embedding symmetry; changing a radio writes the new embedding/symmetry mode.

help.title: Canvas
paragraphs: Double-click empty space to create a zone. Double-click a zone or edge to edit it. Drag a zone to move the selection. Drag empty space to select a group; Ctrl-click adds or removes individual zones.

V: selection mode. E: edge mode. M: magnet mode. To connect quickly, click zone A, hold Shift and click zone B. Shift temporarily selects edge mode. Hold Alt for magnet mode; Alt takes priority over Shift. Release the modifier to return to your chosen mode.

Ctrl while dragging: snap the grabbed zone's center to grid crosses or cell centers (32 units between the two grids). All selected zones keep their relative spacing. Ctrl+A: select all. Delete: remove selection. Enter: edit selection. Esc: clear selection or cancel a pending edge.

Wheel: zoom at the pointer. In Magnet mode, wheel down expands the map frame and wheel up shrinks it, stopping when it fits all zones. Ctrl+wheel still zooms. Middle or right drag: pan. F or Home: fit graph, including the map frame in Magnet mode.

Auto place creates a compact diagram with rectangular boundaries and symmetric rows and columns where topology permits. Grid-like graphs are laid out as grids; irregular graphs use a certified planar construction. Positions snap to grid crosses or cell centers and are checked for node overlaps and edge crossings. Connections leave room for one full dotted pattern at 100% zoom, and the whole graph is fitted into the canvas. The top menu shows (!) for non-planar connection topology; Auto place is disabled until it is fixed. Placement changes only visualizer positions and is one undo step.

help.title: Position magnets
paragraphs: Global settings > Position magnets > Random magnet rotation lets the whole magnet arrangement turn around the map center. The seed chooses one common angle; the same seed and map size repeat it. Forces, distances between targets and distances to the center stay unchanged. Only angles where the entire group stays inside the map are eligible; targets near corners have fewer fitting angles. Moving targets closer to the center or enlarging the editor's map frame allows more angles. The saved diagram stays in its authored orientation.

In Magnet mode, single-click a zone to toggle its own position magnet. Drag instead of releasing to enable it and adjust its force: farther from the zone center increases strength; grabbing off-center and dragging toward the center reduces it. The minimum is 0.1 and remains enabled; only a click or the settings checkbox disables it. Each drag is one undo step and never moves the zone.

A magnet has a red and blue outline with a glow that grows and brightens with its force. Its label shows Magnet force. You can also configure the force in Node settings. This positive positional force is independent of the zone's susceptibility to the existing central magnet.

The square map frame is centered on the bounds of all zone squares. Its minimum size fits every zone, even non-magnets. Wheel changes its padding; Fit frame resets it to the minimum. The frame updates after adding, moving, resizing or auto-placing zones. Panning and camera zoom never change targets. Targets use 0 to 1 coordinates, from top left to bottom right, and are saved with the template. An outside target must not be applied.

Generation uses saved positional targets during initial placement and relaxation. Stronger force keeps a zone closer to its target, independently of susceptibility. The existing central magnet can still attract or repel it. These are soft preferences rather than locks; valid crossings, map bounds and other connections still constrain movement. A template selected for generation is a snapshot: after editing magnets, choose Use for generation again to select the updated settings.

help.title: Files and history
paragraphs: Ctrl+C: copy data from the active zone or connection. Ctrl+V: paste to all selected zones or the selected connection. Copy data and Paste data are also in Edit and the right-click menu. IDs, canvas positions and connections stay unchanged. Edge data includes both directed rules: the source first-to-second rule maps to the destination first-to-second rule. A disabled source direction clears that destination rule. Node and edge clipboards are separate types; incompatible or invalid data is rejected without changes. When several zones are selected, Copy data uses the last clicked zone.

Ctrl+N: new. Ctrl+O: open. Ctrl+S: save. Ctrl+Shift+S: save as. Ctrl+Z: undo. Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z: redo. Ctrl+comma: global settings. Ctrl+Enter: use for generation. Each group move and applied settings menu is one document undo step. Inside a menu, Undo/Redo also works on individual fields, toggles and resource rows before applying.

Undo/redo notifications list changed values as from -> to. Notifications stack and let mouse input pass through to controls below; only each message's x button captures clicks. Click x to dismiss it, or let it fade after four seconds. Hover does not extend its lifetime. Selection and camera navigation do not edit the template.

help.title: Settings menus
paragraphs: Enter applies the menu. Escape, Cancel and the x button close it. If you changed values, a confirmation lets you keep editing or discard them. Hover any (?) marker to learn what that parameter does. F2 opens this help.

help.title: Template basics
paragraphs: A zone is a node with a unique ID, relative radius and magnetic susceptibility. Its resource intervals cover 0 to 1 without gaps or overlaps and color the square from bottom to top. Noise octaves control patch scales; per-zone weights control their contributions.

Edges describe shared border walls, passages and resource blending. Directed rules apply independently from A to B and from B to A. Optional center distances affect generation spacing; drawing a longer edge does not set a generation distance.

Canvas positions are saved as visualizer metadata and never affect generation. Drafts may have isolated zones or nonplanar graphs. Use for generation validates a snapshot and selects it in the Generator tab; later edits require selecting a new snapshot. Canvas coordinates are stored with at most two decimal places.
Save in assets/templates if you want changes to survive CMake configuration. Runtime JSON copies in build/src can be replaced by configuration.
